statement: Venice acquired Ragusa under the Treaty of Zadar (1205) following the Fourth Crusade, maintaining overlordship until 1358 when the Treaty of Zadar (1358) transferred Ragusa to the Kingdom of Hungary-Croatia. Venetian rule gave Ragusa its commercial infrastructure (the Fondaco system, standardized weights and measures) but also subjected it to unfavorable trade restrictions. Ragusa's eventual break from Venice — achieved through Hungarian overlordship — gave it the greater commercial freedom that enabled its 15th-century golden age.
